name: MLP Neural Fields
text:
# MLP Neural Fields

Also called: Neural Implicit Representation

## Overview
MLP Neural Fields define a continuous scene function $F_\Theta: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^k$ using a [Multi-Layer Perceptron](#23740-neural-network-for-transfer-function-parameterization.md) (MLP) to map spatial coordinates (and optionally viewing direction) to signal values such as density and color [G]. This family solves the problem of [implicit scene representation](#19517-implicit-scene-representations.md) by storing network parameters instead of explicit voxels, allowing for infinite resolution reconstruction with memory usage constant relative to spatial resolution [G]. It sets itself apart from sibling methods like [Explicit Neural Feature Volume](1838-explicit-neural-feature-volume.md) and [Hash Grid Neural Fields](3855-hash-grid-neural-fields.md) by relying entirely on the MLP's capacity to learn high-frequency details, whereas those siblings use auxiliary data structures (grids, hash tables) to accelerate queries or store features [G].

## Shared principles

## Subtopics

### [NeRF MLP Architecture](910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md)
The [NeRF MLP Architecture](#910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md) is a multi-layer perceptron that implicitly represents a 3D scene as a continuous volumetric function, mapping 3D spatial coordinates and viewing directions to volume density and view-dependent color. It solves the problem of novel view synthesis by optimizing a neural network to minimize the photometric error between rendered images and ground truth observations. It sets itself apart from its siblings, such as [Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md) which uses a single network for both geometry and appearance without explicit view-dependent bottlenecks, and [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md) which uses periodic sine activations, by employing a two-stage architecture with ReLU activations, positional encoding, and a specific skip-connection structure to enforce multiview consistency (view-independent density, view-dependent color).

### [Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md)
[Scene Representation Networks (SRN)](#1150-scene-representation-networks-srn.md) represent a continuous scene as an opaque surface implicitly defined by a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) that maps 3D coordinates to a feature vector. Unlike standard volume rendering methods that integrate density and color along a ray, SRN uses a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to march along the ray, predicting step sizes until the surface is found, then decoding the final feature vector into a single color. This approach is distinct from its siblings, such as [NeRF MLP Architecture](910-nerf-mlp-architecture.md), which models volumetric density and view-dependent color continuously, whereas [SRN models](#21186-srn-linear.md) a single opaque surface per ray.

### [SIREN Neural Field](1250-siren-neural-field.md)
SIREN ([Sinusoidal Representation Networks](#1250-siren-neural-field.md)) is a coordinate-based [implicit neural representation](#19545-implicit-neural-representation-inr.md) that maps continuous spatial coordinates to signal values (e.g., voxel intensity, density, or color) using a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with sinusoidal activation functions. It solves the problem of representing high-frequency details and computing well-behaved derivatives in neural fields, which standard ReLU-based MLPs fail to do due to spectral bias and zero second derivatives. Unlike [MLP Neural Fields](3854-mlp-neural-fields.md) which typically use ReLU or tanh, SIREN’s periodic activations allow it to capture intricate volumetric structures and fine details that would otherwise be smoothed away.

### [MLP Neural Field](1256-mlp-neural-field.md)
A [plain MLP neural field](#1256-mlp-neural-field.md) maps continuous spatial coordinates to signal values (such as density and color) using a standard Multi-Layer Perceptron with ReLU activations. It serves as the fundamental baseline for coordinate-based neural representations, contrasting with specialized architectures like SIREN that use sinusoidal activations to overcome spectral bias. Unlike voxel-based methods, it offers constant memory usage relative to spatial resolution, enabling infinite-resolution reconstruction.

### [Neural Confidence Field](11343-neural-confidence-field.md)
The [Neural Confidence Field](#11343-neural-confidence-field.md) is a method that augments a standard [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) with an additional output predicting a confidence score $\zeta$ for every sampled point and viewing direction. It solves the problem of joint optimization instability in [Structure-from-Motion (SfM)](#16341-structure-from-motion-sfm.md) scenarios, particularly when camera poses are unknown or inaccurate, by providing a metric to weigh the contribution of rays and poses during training. Unlike [standard NeRF](#979-nerf-volumetric-rendering-coarse-fine-sampling.md) which treats all observations equally, this method distinguishes between reliable and unreliable data, allowing for incremental pose registration and robust optimization.

### Neural Dependence Fields (NDFs)
NDFs learn the statistical dependencies between spatial locations across ensemble members by mapping pairs of 3D coordinates to Pearson correlation or mutual information values [S2, unofficial]. On a 1000-member weather ensemble (250 × 352 × 20), NDFs achieved 87.63 dB PSNR for self-correlation fields with 9 ms inference, 26× faster than GPU-computed Pearson correlation and five orders of magnitude faster than CPU mutual information estimation, at over 6,000× [compression](#4-compression.md) relative to storing all pairwise correlations [S2, unofficial]. The method operates on a single time step and tends to smooth fine-scale correlation structures due to hash table capacity constraints [S2, unofficial].

### Perturbation Field Modeling
This method introduces a parametrized perturbation field $D$ to reparameterize the MLP input coordinates, allowing uncertainty estimation by measuring maximum tolerated perturbation without retraining the base model [S3]. The mode of the posterior distribution is $\omega = 0$, which corresponds to the original unperturbed model performance [S3]. Perturbation field parameters $\omega$ have shape $R^{M \times D}$, where $M$ is the grid size storing displacement vectors and $D$ is the vector dimension [S3]. Medium density and color are assumed constant and are not affected by perturbations [S3].

### Dictionary Fields
[Dictionary Fields](#11944-dictionary-fields.md) factor a neural field into a spatial coefficient field times a shared basis field, using periodic coordinate warping [S4]. This enables multi-signal learning and few-shot or sparse-view reconstruction because the basis captures reusable structure while coefficients remain scene-specific [S4].

### DreamEditor
DreamEditor is a mesh-based representation method for local editing [S5]. It converts the original neural field into a mesh-based representation, back-projects the 2D mask onto the mesh to identify editing regions, and utilizes [SDS](#21179-score-distillation-sampling-sds.md) loss to optimize color and geometry features and vertex positions within the selected regions, facilitating precise [local adjustments](#21587-local-optimization-with-regularization-and-silhouette-fittin.md) [S5].

## Background
The concept of a neural field is defined as a field that is parameterized fully or in part by a neural network, mapping spatio-temporal coordinates to a physical quantity [S1, unofficial]. Feed spatio-temporal coordinates into the neural network to produce the physical quantity [S1, unofficial]. The foundational work on MLP Neural Fields includes Scene Representation Networks (SRN) [S1, unofficial], which used an MLP and RNN for [surface representation](#22781-surface-representation.md), and the baseline MLP Neural Field [S1, unofficial], which demonstrated the spectral bias limitations of standard ReLU networks.
